business_summary: GE Vernova Inc. is the NYSE-listed energy business spun out of General Electric in April 2024. It runs three segments: Power (gas turbines, nuclear services and reactor technology), Electrification (grid solutions, transformers, switchgear, power conversion and storage) and Wind. It is one of a very small number of firms that can supply both the generation asset and the grid equipment that connects it, which is why it is placed on three separate links of this chain.

exposure_summary.narrative: GE Vernova is the only issuer in this batch with three active placements: power-equipment (the money corner), energy-generation and grid-interconnect. That breadth is the exposure and also the caveat, because no single link's demand can be read off the consolidated numbers. The company's second-quarter 2026 release quantifies the data-centre pull directly for Electrification and separately describes gas turbine output capacity ramping through 2030, so both the equipment and the generation legs are disclosed rather than inferred.

disclosed_revenue_exposure.basis: A data-centre revenue percentage is not disclosed. The second-quarter 2026 release (accession 0001996810-26-000147) does disclose a data-centre order figure for Electrification year to date, which is an order intake number, not a revenue share.

crowdedness_caveats: This is the most discovered name in the batch. data/market/GEV.json pcs records 33 analysts and 81.7% institutional ownership as of 2026-08-29, axis-B SATURATED, and the 52-week range in the same file runs from 547.96 to 1174.86, which is a stock that has already been repriced rather than one waiting to be.
Axis-A reads DARK at 88.2 as of 2026-08-29, but the pcs gate state is ADVISORY, so the retail-quiet reading is uncertified and should not be used to argue the name is undiscovered.
Its power-equipment placement is on an UNDISCOVERED link, but link crowdedness and issuer crowdedness are different measurements and this issuer is the one that is crowded.

data_gaps: Net debt to EBITDA is NULL: companyfacts returned no total_debt, no long_term_debt and no cash observation for GE Vernova, so neither leg of net debt exists in the local store.

The reverse DCF did not solve: enterprise value is null in data/market/GEV.json for the same missing debt and cash legs, so implied FCF CAGR and horizon spread are both NULL and this issuer has no expectations-gap reading.
Piotroski is PENDING_DATA on the missing long_term_debt_fy input; Beneish is PENDING_DATA on missing ppe_net_fy and long_term_debt_fy.
Revenue history begins at fiscal 2022 in companyfacts, so the three-year CAGR spans the entire available series and cannot be compared with a pre-spin baseline.
The disclosed data-centre figure is order intake, not revenue, and no revenue share is published.

disposition.basis: Complete medium profile with three filing-backed placements including the money corner, but the weakest measurement set in the batch: no leverage, no earnings quality and no expectations-gap reading because companyfacts has no debt or cash for this issuer. Retained for monitoring; a debt and cash backfill would change the picture materially.

confidence_audit.basis: Counts cover the canonical metric fields only. VERIFIED is a figure read directly off SEC companyfacts as reported. INFERRED is a figure computed from SEC companyfacts, with the derivation named in its basis; where a market price enters the computation the basis says so explicitly, because the price leg is the repo's own dual-source market plane (data/market/GEV.json, price_status AGREED) and not an issuer document. SPECULATIVE is reserved for the reverse-DCF solve, whose discount rate and terminal growth are assumed. NULL is a field looked for and not found, never estimated.
